questions.question: Analyse the usefulness of cash flow forecasts for a seasonal retail business operating a brick-and-mortar store.
questions.modelAnswer: Cash flow forecasts help identify upcoming liquidity gaps during quiet months (e.g., post-Christmas), allowing the business to arrange overdrafts early.
questions.reasoning: 2 marks for knowledge of cash flow, 3 marks for context application, 3 marks for analytical consequences.

questions.question: Evaluate whether raising finance through a share issue (equity) is always better than taking out a bank loan (debt) for a growing manufacturing enterprise.
questions.modelAnswer: Equity does not require interest repayments and doesn't increase gearing, reducing financial risk. However, it dilutes existing ownership control, whereas debt preserves control but adds fixed interest burdens.
questions.reasoning: Award 4 marks for understanding methods, 4 marks for comparative analysis, and 2 marks for conclusion.

questions.question: Assess the benefits of lean production methods for a car manufacturing business.
questions.modelAnswer: Lean production reduces waste, lowers holding costs through just-in-time (JIT), and improves overall product quality by catching defects early.
questions.reasoning: Award up to 2 marks for knowledge of lean production, 2 marks for application, and 4 marks for balanced analysis.

questions.question: Evaluate the importance of quality assurance compared to quality control for a global food processing company.
questions.modelAnswer: Quality assurance builds quality into every stage of production, preventing errors proactively. Quality control catches faults at the end, which leads to higher waste if batch failures occur.
questions.reasoning: Award 4 marks for conceptual knowledge, 4 marks for comparative analysis, and 2 marks for evaluation.
